title: Batching entropy sleuth log
content:
Summary:
Observed a sustained ~30-45% throughput drop for a subset of requests (mostly short chatbot style, 32-128 token responses) starting 2026-02-25 ~03:40 UTC. Latency P50/P95 increased slightly but the primary pain is reduced token/sec on dedicated pools using continuous-batcher (cbatch) path. Errors are low; SLOs failing because cost per convo spiked.

This doc is my running scratchpad as I triage. Notes are messy — stepping through investigations, commands I ran, raw snippets, and hypotheses.

Environment/context:
- Affected: dedicated pool gp-dedicated-2 (NVLink A100 equivalent), model family: rw-13b-lvt (fp16), continuous-batcher enabled with warmup and kv-prefetch toggles.
- Not affected: burst-only / non-cbatch pools; inference via hosted-api fallback unchanged.
- First regression signal: 2026-02-25 03:40 UTC from console per-route tokens/sec alert (route: chat-latency), alert threshold 20% drop.
- Recent config changes (rolling): 2026-02-24 22:12 UTC: autoscaler config tweak; 2026-02-25 01:05 UTC: cbatch default window ms bumped 4->6ms in rollout-2026-02-25-01.

High-level hypothesis (short):
Something in the continuous-batcher window or KV prefetch interaction caused batch coalescing to become suboptimal for typical short-chat load, increasing wait time per request and reducing effective throughput. Potential boundary: small increase in window (4->6ms) + slight skew in arrival distribution -> longer tail for batch completion and decreased batching density due to earlier flush heuristics. Also suspect the recent kernel selection change (PR #1987) might have altered warmup/cold-path behavior.

Timeline / what I checked so far:
- 2026-02-25 04:10 UTC: Pulled per-node cbatch metrics (cbatch.batch_size_distribution, cbatch.wait_time_ms) from metrics store for affected pool.
  - Found: median batch size dropped from ~6.8 -> ~4.1; 95th percentile wait_time_ms increased from ~1.2ms -> ~3.8ms.
- 2026-02-25 04:25 UTC: Verified no JVM/OS-level resource saturation (CPU, mem, NVLink) on nodes. Everything nominal.
- 2026-02-25 04:40 UTC: Rolled back window ms to 4ms on a small canary subset (2 nodes). Observed partial recovery (~+12% tokens/sec) for canary within 10 minutes.
- 2026-02-25 05:10 UTC: Re-enabled cbatch logging with debug sampling at 5% for affected pool.
- 2026-02-25 08:50 UTC: Correlated kv-cache hit/miss rates — no large change. However KV prefetch queue length spiked intermittently (short bursts).

Commands / queries I ran (note: ad-hoc, copy-paste friendly):
- Metrics query (prometheus-ish):
  sum(rate(cbatch_tokens_generated_total{pool=\"gp-dedicated-2\",route=\"chat-latency\"}[5m])) by (instance)
- Check batch size distribution:
  histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(cbatch_batch_size_bucket{pool=\"gp-dedicated-2\"}[5m])) by (le))
- Inspect node mem/pmem/cuda: ssh node && nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory --format=csv
- Tail debug logs for cbatch: kubectl -n serving logs -l app=continuous-batcher -c cbatcher --since=2h | grep -E \"batch_size|wait_time|flush\" -n

Representative log snippets (redacted IDs):
- 2026-02-25T03:46:12.234Z cbatch INFO batch_start id=aa12 size=3 wait_ms=5.2 flush_reason=timeout
- 2026-02-25T03:46:12.235Z runtime WARN kv_prefetch queue_len=18 prefetch_latency_ms=12.4
- 2026-02-25T03:46:12.236Z cbatch INFO batch_dispatch id=aa12 size=3 target_shard=shard-9
- 2026-02-25T03:46:12.481Z runtime INFO token_emit node=ip-10-3-4-9 tokens=64 latency_ms=245

Notes from logs: repeated pattern where cbatch flush_reason=timeout shows up more often (previously flush_reason=size_reached). Batches are smaller and more frequent timeouts. Prefetch queue spikes line up with timeout events.

Hypotheses (detailed):
1) Window increase reduced chance for short coincident requests to coalesce; because arrival distribution has tightened, an extra 2ms creates misalignment with sample-based flushing heuristics -> more timeout flushes. (Evidence: median batch size drop, rollback improved throughput).
2) KV prefetch interaction: when prefetch queue length grows, runtime signals backpressure that delays processing and causes cbatch to see longer waits and earlier timeout flushes; prefetch bursts could be due to slightly changed kernel warmup behavior in PR #1987. (Evidence: prefetch latency spikes; log correlation).
3) Kernel selection PR (#1987) changed latency characteristics for cold paths such that small batches have slightly higher per-batch overhead leading to preference for larger batches, but rollout toggles misaligned and caused temporary bump in overhead for small batches which then reduced throughput. (Evidence: warmup counters show more cold-path hits after 2026-02-24).

Quick experiments and outcomes:
- Rolled back window on canary nodes -> partial recovery (~12%).
- Temporarily disabled kv-prefetch on one node -> batch_size rebounded to ~6.5, tokens/sec recovered ~18% locally. However disabling prefetch caused slight tail latency increase for some long convo tests.
- Reverted PR #1987 on single node (via kernel selection override) -> inconclusive due to noise; needs longer run.

Risk assessment:
- Global rollback of window param seems low-risk (we rolled it back previously), but it might hide root cause if there is deeper interaction with kv-prefetch and warmup.
- Disabling kv-prefetch globally may reduce throughput variance short-term but could regress latency for long-tail requests and reduce cache effectiveness.
- PR #1987 revert requires CI/QA and coordination with release-engineering; medium risk and likely higher blast radius.

Immediate next steps (ordered):
1) Rollback window ms to 4ms across affected pool progressively (complete within next 2 hours) and monitor tokens/sec + batch size metrics. -> Done? partially; finish rollout.
2) Increase cbatch debug sampling to 25% for 2 hours post-rollback to validate persistent recovery and to collect richer traces. (Maya: can you help flip sampling?)
3) Run controlled A/B: one node group with kv-prefetch disabled, matched load replay for 30m to measure tradeoffs (Arjun to orchestrate).
4) Instrument warmup counters per shard to see if PR #1987 correlates with cold-path regressions. Add metric: runtime.warmup_cold_path_hits_by_shard. (Follow up PR if missing.)
5) If rollback restores throughput and kv-prefetch A/B shows improvement when disabled, schedule a deeper postmortem and plan for safer prefetch backpressure throttling.

Ideas for longer-term fixes / guardrails:
- Add automated canary for cbatch window changes that compares median batch size and wait_time_ms on canary vs baseline before rollout continues.
- Make kv-prefetch queue size self-throttle when cbatch wait_time_ms crosses threshold to avoid circular backpressure.
- Add dashboards that combine batch_size distribution + kv_prefetch queue histogram + kernel_warmup_rate so we can triage quicker next time.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Why did arrival distribution tighten around 03:40 UTC? Could be change in client-side retry/backoff behavior or a downstream traffic shift. Check gateway logs for per-route QPS microbursts.
- Need to confirm if rollout schedule for PR #1987 aligns with other infra changes (autoscaler tweak earlier same night).
- Confirm that our cbatch flush_reason metrics are capturing 'prefetch_backpressure' type reasons (if not, add).
- Is there a way to emit sample of original arrival timestamps to compute inter-arrival hist for short requests? Would help validate hypothesis 1.

Raw snippets for postmortem (copy as-is):
- metric delta summary (affected pool): tokens/sec: baseline 138k -> 88k at trough; median batch size 6.8 -> 4.1; wait_time_ms median 1.2 -> 3.8; kv_prefetch queue median 2 -> 9.
- last config changes: rollout-2026-02-24-22:12 autoscaler tweak (no cbatch changes); rollout-2026-02-25-01:05 cbatch.window_ms 4->6. PR refs: #1987 kernel selection.

If reading later: TL;DR — small window bump + kv-prefetch/backpressure interaction appears most likely. Rolling window back to 4ms and A/B disabling prefetch give strong signals. Plan: finish rollback, run A/B, collect richer traces, then design throttling to avoid prefetch -> cbatch feedback loop.

-- Leah

(End of scratchpad)
